supporting_article_titles: Manus 2.0 and Cue give AI agents their own email, phone and wallet
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: AI agents can now operate with their own email, phone, wallet and computer, make budget-bounded payments, receive calls and collaborate, moving agents from chat-only assistants toward externally acting operational identities.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: agent deployment → identity/channel assignment → permission and spend limits → external action → evidence/review
raw_opportunities.target_customer: SMBs and operations teams deploying autonomous agents for customer, procurement or administrative tasks
raw_opportunities.buyer: operations manager, finance controller or AI program owner
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: govern agent identities, budgets, external communications and irreversible actions without losing accountability
raw_opportunities.current_friction: As agents gain phone/email/wallet access, permissions, spend caps, action ownership and audit evidence become fragmented across agent platforms and connected services.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: vendor-neutral agent identity and authority register with per-agent budgets, approved channels/actions, human-approval rules and exported action ledger
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A lightweight control desk that records what each autonomous agent is allowed to contact, spend and execute, then keeps an auditable action trail.
raw_opportunities.why_now: Cue gives agents operational identities and wallets and Manus 2.0 adds event-triggered automation, materially increasing the number of externally acting agent workflows.
raw_opportunities.evidence_notes: Manus primary launch post confirms email, phone, wallet, computer, budget-bounded payments and multi-agent handoff; TNW independently reports launch and metrics.

supporting_article_titles: Daimler Truck: concerned about using cash to avoid new NoX rules
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: A pending U.S. EPA 2027 NOx regime may preserve a tight 0.035 g/hp-hr standard while allowing non-conformance penalties, creating a concrete comply-vs-penalty economic decision for manufacturers and fleets.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: vehicle/engine option → compliance rule → engineering or acquisition premium → penalty/exposure scenario → procurement decision
raw_opportunities.target_customer: U.S. heavy-duty fleet procurement teams, truck dealers and smaller engine/vehicle suppliers
raw_opportunities.buyer: fleet procurement director, compliance manager or commercial planning team
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: compare 2027 NOx-compliant vehicle/engine choices against regulatory cost and uncertainty scenarios
raw_opportunities.current_friction: Rule details are pending and costs differ between compliant technology and possible penalties, leaving procurement assumptions scattered across regulatory text and spreadsheets.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: versioned NOx rule scenario calculator with vehicle counts, compliant premium, possible NCP assumptions, timing and decision memo export
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A 2027 U.S. heavy-truck NOx procurement scenario desk that turns changing rule assumptions into fleet cost comparisons.
raw_opportunities.why_now: Daimler has already engineered a compliant Detroit 6 while publicly objecting to proposed NCP economics; the final rule remains pending ahead of 2027.
raw_opportunities.evidence_notes: FreightWaves reports the pending EPA amendments, Daimler's compliant engine and concern that NCPs could alter economic incentives.

supporting_article_titles: Versicherer: Allianz-Manager warnt - „KI-Risiken nicht vollständig versicherbar“
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: Allianz Commercial says AI can create correlated accumulation risks that are not fully insurable, including dependency on a small number of model providers and AI-related losses spreading across existing insurance lines.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: AI use/dependency inventory → shared-provider concentration mapping → business-process criticality → loss scenario → mitigation/insurance discussion
raw_opportunities.target_customer: mid-market companies materially dependent on external AI/model providers
raw_opportunities.buyer: risk manager, CFO, CIO or insurance broker
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: identify hidden AI concentration risk across business processes before insurance renewal or resilience planning
raw_opportunities.current_friction: Companies may list AI tools but do not aggregate which critical processes depend on the same model/provider, making correlated outage or liability exposure hard to evidence.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: AI dependency register linking provider/model to business processes, criticality, fallback, data exposure and concentration heatmap with broker-ready export
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: An AI concentration-risk register that shows when many critical company workflows quietly depend on the same model or provider.
raw_opportunities.why_now: Allianz Commercial explicitly warns that provider concentration can create simultaneous losses across customers and that AI risks increasingly cut across existing insurance products.
raw_opportunities.evidence_notes: Handelsblatt interview directly quotes Allianz Commercial CEO on uninsurable accumulation risk, model-provider dependency and AI risk permeating existing products.
